kill_fact: There is no asymmetry to buy, and the record's own middle case is too generous. The catalyst itself checks out: it is live and has not fired. The Q3 2026 8-K (Ex. 99.1, 10 November 2026) and the 10-Q filed the same day both say top-line OPERA-01 data are expected in the first quarter of 2027, with the NDA in 2027 and a potential launch in 2028. That is a reiteration, not a slip. But it is still a guided quarter for an event-driven, blinded-review read-out. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06016738, read 16 November 2026, still shows primary completion 31 October 2026 as ESTIMATED, last update posted 13 August 2026, and statusVerifiedDate 2025-08, so the data cut-off is not publicly confirmed. The load-bearing error is in the numbers. The record values the ESR1-mutant-only outcome (weighted 43%, its most likely favourable branch) at $7.00, as an entrant into a market holding 'approved elacestrant and approved imlunestrant with abemaciclib'. The FDA record is different: imlunestrant (Inluriyo) was approved as a MONOTHERAPY for ESR1-mutated 2L+ disease on 25 September 2025, and vepdegestrant (Veppanu) was approved for the same population on 1 May 2026. A mutant-only palazestrant label in 2028 would therefore be the FOURTH oral single-agent degrader in that niche, after elacestrant, imlunestrant and vepdegestrant. The record counts two approved rivals. Vepdegestrant's sponsors had still not chosen a commercial partner at approval, which shows how thin the economics are for a late entrant there. Re-cutting that branch to about $5.50 (about $2.45 of net cash plus about $3 for a 4th-entrant franchise and the early pipeline), and trimming the both-halves value for the same crowding in its ESR1-mutant slice, gives an event-win value of about $14.75. The probability-weighted value becomes 0.22 x 14.75 + 0.43 x 5.50 + 0.35 x 2.45 = about $6.47, below the $7.13 price. The verified floor is about $2.45, 66% lower. At $7.13 the market already implies about a 38% chance of the both-halves win ((7.13 - 2.45) / (14.75 - 2.45)), an outcome no oral SERD has achieved as a single agent in ESR1-wild-type disease (acelERA missed; EMBER-3 monotherapy missed the overall population at HR 0.87, p = 0.12). The floor and the event are real. The spread is not.
corrections:
1) MATERIAL - competitive set in the ESR1-mutant branch. The record lists elacestrant plus 'imlunestrant with abemaciclib' as the approved rivals. The FDA approved imlunestrant monotherapy for ER+/HER2- ESR1-mutated advanced breast cancer after at least one endocrine line on 25 September 2025 (Guardant360 CDx companion). It also approved vepdegestrant (Veppanu) for the same population on 1 May 2026 (VERITAC-2: PFS 5.0 vs 2.1 months, HR 0.57). A mutant-only palazestrant would be the 4th approved oral single agent there by its 2028 launch, so the $7.00 middle case and the $250-350m peak-sales assumption are too high. Re-cut: mutant-only branch about $5.50; both-halves event-win about $14.75 (palazestrant ex-cash cut from about $11.30 to about $9.55 per share on about $850m peak instead of $1.0bn at the same about 1.14x multiple, plus $2.45 net cash, $1.50 OP-3136 and $1.25 OPERA-02 read-through); probability-weighted value about $6.47 against $7.13.
2) MATERIAL (in the bull's favour, now superseded) - the previous skeptic pass (9 November) said the Q3 report was scheduled for 20 November and that the guidance had not been reiterated. Both are wrong as of today. Olema filed its Q3 8-K (Items 2.02/9.01) and 10-Q on 10 November 2026, and both reaffirm Q1 2027 top-line data. The record's 10 November dating is correct.
3) MINOR - floor verified. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $413.771m and total liabilities $72.233m at 30 September 2026 (total current liabilities $69.233m). Q3 net loss was $73.599m, including $12.1m non-cash stock-based compensation ($7.7m R&D + $4.4m G&A). That puts the cash operating cost at about $65m a quarter, against about $4m of interest income. Rolling net working capital forward 1.5 quarters to mid-Q1 2027 gives about $250m over 101.2m economic shares (87,606,263 common plus 13,594,149 pre-funded warrants at $0.0001 as of 5 November 2026) = about $2.47 a share. The record's $2.45 stands.
4) MINOR - 'no going-concern warning' needs a footnote. Management's formal conclusion is that cash is sufficient for at least 12 months, and the 10-Q states a runway 'through mid-2028', which is verified. But the 10-Q risk factors do say these conditions 'raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern over the long term.' That is not a near-term financing risk before the read-out.
5) MINOR - Novartis change-of-control toll verified from the 10-Q (Note 10), now first-hand rather than second-hand. A third-party change of control or compound transaction triggers a 'Repayment Amount' of a pro-rata share of approximately $275m, set by the units of ribociclib actually supplied for OPERA-02 against the total that could be supplied. Because OPERA-02 is still enrolling, the toll on a near-term takeover is a fraction of $275m, not the full amount. Novartis also holds rights of first negotiation and first offer and must be notified of any sale process.
6) MINOR - 12 November 8-K: name change to Olema Oncology, Inc. and an HQ move to South San Francisco only. No timing content.
